question: In the Modern Periodic Table, Tellurium (atomic number 52) is surrounded by elements with atomic numbers:
solution:
The correct answer is __**34, 51, 53, 84**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tellurium's symbol is **Te **and atomic number is **52**.
 
• It is a rare metalloid found in ores like **gold **and **silver tellurides**.
 
• Used in **thermoelectric **devices, **semiconductors**, and **alloys**.
 
• It appears **silvery-white**, **brittle**, and **metallic**.
 
• Tellurium compounds have a garlic-like odor and are **toxic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the modern periodic table metals, metalloids and nonmetals are found in the **p-block** which is on the right-hand side of the chart.
 
• Metalloids are those elements possessing properties between nonmetals and metals.
 
• These are also known as semi-metals.
 
• They have a **metallic appearance** with the brittle property of non-metals.
 
• They show average conductance and most of their chemical properties resemble the non-metals.
 
• The elements which are metalloids in the periodic table are boron, silicon, arsenic, antimony, polonium, and carbon.
 
• Metalloids are **semiconductors**.
